papers.title: Experimental and Numerical Study of Heat Source Modeling for Keyhole Formation in Ti-6Al-4V Single Pass Laser Treatment
papers.abstract: Abstract This study analyses the impact of laser surface treatment on Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy using an air-cooled ytterbium fiber laser system. The alloy’s microstructure, consisting of α and β phases, was processed at different laser powers (80 W, 90 W, 100 W) while maintaining a constant scanning speed. Through microscopic analysis, hardness testing and phase evolution observations, the results revealed notable microstructural changes, particularly the formation of a martensitic Ti-oxide layer. Numerical simulations were conducted using the SFTC DEFORM-3D™ software, which modelled the laser heat source and thermal behaviour, along with a custom subroutine for predicting hardness and phase transformations. The study specifically examined molten pool geometry, Ti-oxide layer thickness and the hardness distribution on the treated surface. Several heat source models were tested, with the Gaussian polynomial curve model providing the most accurate results for simulating keyhole formation, phase transitions and hardness variations. The findings revealed that increasing laser power significantly affected the thermal and mechanical properties of the material, providing crucial insights for selecting the most appropriate thermal heat source model and optimizing laser surface treatment parameters for enhanced performance. Furthermore, the research proposes a new approach for modelling the heat source based on process temperature, as opposed to traditional geometric heat flux models. This study contributes to the broader field of laser-based manufacturing by advancing numerical modelling techniques aimed at improving the mechanical properties and functional behaviour of Ti-6Al-4V components.

summary_en.motivation: To analyze the impact of laser surface treatment on Ti-6Al-4V microstructure and hardness, focusing on heat source modeling for keyhole formation.

summary_en.result: The Gaussian polynomial curve model provided the most accurate predictions for keyhole geometry, phase transitions, and hardness distribution.
summary_en.validation: Experimental characterization of microstructure, oxide layer thickness, and hardness validated the numerical model.

papers.title: Hydrojet Surface Treatment of Ti-6Al-4V Titanium Produced by Additive Manufacturing
papers.abstract: The aim of this study was to analyze the effect of finishing methods on the surface quality of Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy additively manufactured by selective laser melting. It was observed that among the finishing methods, water jet treatment did not produce significant changes, while the abrasive water jet proved effective in removing defects and smoothing the surface, especially at a pressure of 30 MPa. However, the risk of abrasive particle entrapment in the material was observed. Promising results were also obtained using the water-ice jet, which combines effective material removal with surface smoothing. The selection of the finishing method should be tailored to the application requirements. Further research will focus on optimization and the combination of techniques to improve the functional properties of titanium components.

papers.title: Dissimilar joining of Ti-6Al-4 V with ZK60 and AZ31 by eutectic-melting-induced liquid metal dealloying
papers.abstract: • Dissimilar commercial alloys joined for the first time via dealloying. • Ti and Mg alloys joined via bicontinuous structure without intermetallic layers. • Dealloying based joining enabled dissimilar joint with 3% ductility. • Minor alloying elements can inhibit dealloying-based joining process. Ti-6Al-4V and Mg alloys (ZK60 and AZ31) were successfully joined using a dealloying-based method. The interfacial microstructure and mechanical properties of joints were characterized by scanning electron microscopy, scanning-transmission electron microscopy, energy-dispersive X-ray analysis, indentation testing, and tensile testing. When ZK60 was butt-joined to a Ti-Cu interlayer pre-diffusion bonded to the Ti alloy and heated under pressure, eutectic-melting-induced liquid metal dealloying (EMI-LMD) occurred at the interface. This process led to the formation of a bicontinuous Ti/Mg microstructure, resulting in robust mechanical joining between the dissimilar alloys. Specific minor elements in the Mg alloy significantly influenced the occurrence of dealloying. Dealloying did not occur between the Ti-Cu interlayer and AZ31 due to the formation of an Al-rich diffusion barrier. To address this issue, dealloying-based joining was achieved by inserting ZK60 between the Ti-Cu interlayer and AZ31. EMI-LMD induced a concentration gradient of minor elements in the Mg alloy, which affected the joint properties. This study is the first to demonstrate that the EMI-LMD joining method can be applied to joining dissimilar commercial alloys.

summary_en.motivation: To develop a dealloying-based method for joining Ti-6Al-4V with Mg alloys without forming brittle intermetallic layers.
summary_en.method: Eutectic-melting-induced liquid metal dealloying (EMI-LMD) was used to create a bicontinuous Ti/Mg microstructure at the interface.
summary_en.result: Dissimilar joints of Ti-6Al-4V with ZK60 were achieved with 3% ductility, while joining with AZ31 was hindered by an Al-rich barrier.
summary_en.validation: Microstructural characterization (SEM, STEM, EDS) and mechanical testing (indentation, tensile) were performed.

papers.title: Impact of Cryogenic Cooling on Burnishing of Ti-6AI-4V: An Optimization Approach
papers.abstract: The present study investigates the influence of cryogenic cooling on the burnishing process of Ti-6Al-4V, a widely utilized titanium alloy in aerospace and biomedical applications. While conventional burnishing enhances surface integrity by inducing compressive residual stresses and improving hardness, excessive heat generation limits its effectiveness. Cryogenic-assisted burnishing, incorporating liquid nitrogen as a cooling medium, presents a promising alternative to mitigate thermal softening and enhance mechanical properties. This study systematically optimizes the burnishing process using the Taguchi method, evaluating the effects of key parameters like speed, feed rate, depth of cut, and number of passes on surface roughness and microhardness. Results indicate that cryogenic process significantly enhances hardness, with improvements of up to 31.5% compared to normal counterpart. However, cryogenic conditions also led to elevated surface roughness, with the maximum Ra increasing from 0.347 μm (normal) to 1.17 μm under extreme cooling (-196 °C) due to embrittlement and lower plastic deformation at ultra-low temperatures. These results highlight theºritical need for process optimization to balance mechanical enhancement with surface finish degradation. The study provides actionable insights into the cryogenic burnishing of Ti-6Al- 4V and demonstrates its potential as a superior surface modification strategy for high-performance engineering applications. Major Findings: Cryogenic burnishing of Ti-6Al-4V enhanced microhardness by 31.5% through suppressed thermal softening and improved strain hardening but increased surface roughness due to embrittlement and limited plastic deformation at ultralow temperatures. Taguchi optimization helps balance these effects, enhancing applicability in aerospace and biomedical fields.

summary_en.motivation: To improve surface integrity of Ti-6Al-4V by mitigating thermal softening during burnishing through cryogenic cooling.
summary_en.method: Taguchi optimization was applied to evaluate the effects of cryogenic burnishing parameters (speed, feed, depth of cut, number of passes) on surface roughness and microhardness.
summary_en.result: Cryogenic burnishing increased microhardness by up to 31.5% compared to conventional burnishing but led to higher surface roughness due to embrittlement.
summary_en.validation: Experimental measurements of microhardness and surface roughness validated the process performance.
